This is a Cask ACS machine. I have lots of experience on that machine, AMA if you like.

Well, I didn't design it, just ran and maintained it, but here's my understanding. The fill tubing needs to be a certain diameter so as not to create excessive foam (tube too small) or let the beer become warm or flat in the hose (too large). A larger tube will also increase the drips from the nozzles between fill cycles, increasing oxygen pickup.

One fill tube per can would bottleneck the machine. The speed of this canner is 30-35 cans per minute. The seamer should be the bottleneck for this process.

You have .light rules in the CSS which are overriding the night mode.

Change this:

.light #container {
 background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8);
}

To this:

.light #container {
 background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8);
}

Or just remove all of the .light CSS rules.

I sell fitness and wellness trackers as part of my job. I also own a few. The answer I always give is that if you are into fitness AND are a geek for data, then yes they are more than worth it. Now I don't think you need to go all out on a Fenix 3 (>$500) but a Polar tracker would probably fit your bill quite nicely: they will track heart rate with a chest strap even while underwater (it stores the data and sync's once you're out of the water).
